full_judgment:
7. Mr Abdus Salam Mamun, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the accused-petitioner, submits that the present accused-petitioner being a contractor is not a public servant, and, as such, the impugned proceeding initiated against the accused-petitioner under sections 409/109 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not maintainable in the eye of law. Learned Advocate, in support of his, submissions, has relied on the decisions in the cases of State vs Iqbal Hossain reported in 48 DLR (AD) 100, Khurshid Alam vs Azizur Rahman reported in 9 BLC (AD) 241, Md Joiatiur Rahman vs State reported in 19 BLD 607 = 4 BLC 375, Golam (Md) Abdul Awal Sarkar vs State reported in 49 DLR 95, Abul Basher vs State reported in 47 DLR 521, Abdul Ali vs State reported in 30 DLR (SC) 58, and Taslima Khatoon Chhanda vs State, reported in 17 BLC 277. He next submits that there are 3 accused in the present case and out of 3 accused, accused No.1 Col. Oli Ahmed was. the then Minister, but the case lodged against him was withdrawn by the Government and learned Divisional Special Judge accorded permission to the withdrawal of the case and the case initiated against another accused Md Nurul Anowar, Chairman of Harala Union Parishad was quashed by a Division Bench of this Court in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 9804 of2003, and, as such, there is no public servant in this case at present, and, as such, the proceeding pending against accused Md Yunus, the Chairman of Harala Union Parishad, who is admittedly not a public servant is not maintainable in the eye of law. He then submits that since no money or property was not entrusted to the accused-petitioner, the question of committing the offence of criminal breach of trust does not arise at all, and, as such, the proceeding brought against the accused-petitioner under section 409 is not maintainable. In support of his contentions, he has relied on the decisions in the cases of Lutfar Rahman vs State reported in 25 DLR (AD) 101, Md Moslem Uddin vs State reported in 10 MLR 199, Rafique (Md) vs Syed Morshed Hossain reported in 50 DLR (AD) 163, Lutfar Rahman vs State reported in 21 DLR 933, He points out that the proceeding against one of the 3 accused was withdrawn and the proceeding against another accused was quashed by this Court, and under this circumstances, the impugned proceeding pending only against the present accused-petitioner, the contractor as abettor is not maintainable in the eye of law. The learned Advocate, in support of his contentions, has referred to the decision in the case of Moyna Miali vs State reported in 5 BLD (AD) 99. Learned Advocate for the petitioner opposing the submission of the learned Advocate for opposite party No.2, has added that the impugned proceeding may be quashed even after framing of charge and also after conclusion of the trial of the case if circumstances demand. Learned Advocate, in support of his submissions, has referred to the decisions in the cases of OK-Kyunm-Ok vs State reported in 18 BLC 621, Taslima Khatoon Chhanda vs State reported in 17 BLC 277, State vs Md Nasim reported in 57 DLR (AD) 114, Sher Ali (Md) vs State reported in 46 DLR (AD) 67, Moudud Ahmed vs State reported in 48 DLR (AD) 42. He further submits that since the prosecution materials do not disclose any ingredients of entrustment and fraudulent mens rea to deceive the Government, and, as such, considering all the aspects of the case, the impugned proceeding initiated against the accused-petitioner should be quashed. Mr Mamun lastly submits that since the accused-petitioner is a contractor and that he is not a public servant, the Divisional special Judge has got no jurisdiction to hold trial against him under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code, which are not schedule offences of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, and, as such, the impugned proceeding is of without jurisdiction, that is, coram non-judice, and, as such, the impugned proceeding should be quashed at this moment 

 8. On the other hand, Mr Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the Durniti Daman Commission very vehemently opposes the submissions advanced by the learned Advocate for the accused-petitioner. He submits that the allegations contained in the prosecution materials prima-facie disclose the offences against the accused-petitioner and others under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code and that the allegations brought the accused-petitioner and others are the disputed questions of fact, and that this Court sitting in a jurisdiction under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not in a position to determine the factual aspects of the case unless the evidence is recorded and considered, and considering this aspect of the case, the impugned proceeding should not be quashed. He next submits that charge was framed against the accused-petitioner under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code and the accused-petitioner remaining present before the Court pleaded innocence and prayed for trial in accordance with law, and, as such, it is the duty of the accused-petitioner to prove the case by adducing evidence before the trial Court, and, as such, the impugned proceeding started against the accused-petitioner should not be quashed. He then submits that though FIR named accused No.1 Colonel Oli Ahmed’s case was withdrawn by the Government, but the fact remains that this fact was not within the knowledge of the learned Advocate for the Durniti Daman Commission and the Durniti Daman Commission as well and that another accused Nurul Anowar, whose case was quashed by this Court did not implead the Durniti Daman Commission as opposite-party in that Miscellaneous case, and, as such, the judgment and order passed in miscellaneous case by another Division Bench was beyond the knowledge of the Durniti Daman Commission, and under this circumstances, the Anti-Corruption Commission has taken decision to challenge the Judgment and order passed in favour of above 2 accused before the higher forum in accordance with law, and, as such the judgment and order passed in another miscellaneous case by another Division Bench is not binding upon this Division Bench. He also points out that though the 2 accused, that is, the two public servants have been discharged from the case, even then the present accused-petitioner, the contractor being agent of the department of the Roads and High ways of the Government should not be discharged from the case and the impugned proceeding should not be quashed since the breach of trust following the alleged misappropriation occurred in the way of his business as agent, and, as such, the impugned proceeding brought against the accused-petitioner under section 409 of the Penal Code, which is a schedule offence under the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 should not be quashed. Learned Advocate, in support of his contentions, has relied on the decision in the case of State vs Niren Das Gupta reported in 1957 Criminal Law Journal page 124 (Volume 58 CN 40) (Calcutta High Court). Mr Khan lastly submits that from the attending facts and circumstances of the case, that the accused-petitioner who received the work order as principal accused is promised-bound and under obligation to complete the work and hand over the same to the authority, but failed, and, as such, the present accused-petitioner is not the abettor, rather he is a principal accused against whom the impugned proceeding under section 409 of the Penal Code is very much maintainable, and under this circumstances, the legal decision referred to by the learned Advocate for the accused-petitioner passed in the case of Moyna Miah vs State 5 BLD (AD) 99 is not applicable in the present proceeding, and, as such, the impugned proceeding should not be quashed. 

 18. Now question comes for consideration as to whether the prosecution materials on record prima-facie disclose offence against the accused- petitioner under section 409 of the Penal Code. In order to come to a decision on this issue, we have gone through the contention of FIR, charge-sheet and other materials on record. It appears from the FIR that the present accused-petitioner along with 2 others as per allegation made in the FIR did not complete the proposed building which was supposed to be completed within 90 days from the date of work order. It is alleged in the FIR that work order for construction of the building was issued on 31-12-1994 and the building was supposed to be constructed on 10-3-1995, that is, within 90 days from the date of work order. It may be mentioned that the accused-petitioner received money amounting to Taka 40,38,779, but the construction work was not completed within that period. The investigating officer after holding investigation submitted charge-sheet against the accused-petitioner and others under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act,1947 holding the view that they got prima-facie case against the accused-petitioner and others for committing the offence of criminal breach of trust as alleged in the FIR. The learned Special Judge on receiving of the case framed charge against the accused petitioner and others under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. The accused-petitioner and others being present before the Court pleaded innocence and prayed for trial in accordance 'with law. On consideration of the prosecution materials on record, we find that a prima-facie case has been disclosed against the accused-petitioner under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code, which ate triable under the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. 

 19. It is a settled principle of law that the disputed questions of fact cannot be decided invoking the jurisdiction under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and it is the function of the trial Court which will decide the factual aspects of the case on taking evidence. It is also a settled principle of law that in a proceeding under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, this Court should not draw an inquiry as to the truth or otherwise of the fact which is not in the proceeding. It is also well-settled that when the allegation brought against the accused-petitioner appears to be so preposterous and absurd or even on the admitted facts no case stands against the accused, in that case this Court invoking its jurisdiction under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure can quash any proceeding. Here, in the instant case, the accused-petitioner received the work order for construction of the bhaban on 31-12-1994. As per terms and conditions of the work order, the accused-petitioner was supposed to complete the: three storied building within 90 days from the date of work order, but that construction work had not been completed within the stipulated period of time. The accused-petitioner, in collaboration with each other, constructed the building upto the I s floor and received bills to the tune of Taka 40,38,779. Thereafter, the accused-petitioner and others intentionally having malafide intention did not hand over the building to the concerned authority by constructing the same in due time as per terms and conditions of the work order. Under the circumstances, we are of the view that the hard earned money of the people spent from the public exchequer cannot be misused at the whims and sweet wills of the accused-petitioner and others for their illegal gains and benefits. The Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 (now repealed) indicates that if any public servant or any other person who in collaboration with each other commits the offences punishable under sections 403 to 409, 417 to 420, 465 to 468,471 and 477 A of the Penal Code, he or she may be tried under the appropriate provisions of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. It may be mentioned that the alleged occurrence took place during the period from September, 1994 to June, 1995. Having glimpsed at the schedule appended to the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, we find that the offence under section 409 of the Penal Code was a schedule offence before amendment of schedule of the Act in 2004. At present, the offence under section 409 of the Penal Code alleged to have been committed by the accused-petitioner is also a schedule offence both under the, Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and the Duniti Daman Commission Act, 2004. 

 20. Accordingly, on going through the FIR, charge-sheet arid other prosecution materials on record, we are led to hold that a prima-facie case has been disclosed against the accused-petitioner, which is triable under the provisions of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and punish- able under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code. 

 (c) Whether the impugned proceeding may be proceeded against the accused-petitioner under section 409 'of the Penal Code in the absence of any public servant as defined in, section 21 of the Penal Code and section 2(b) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958? 

 26. The aforesaid view also finds support the decision in the case of State vs Niren Das Gupta and others reported in 1957 Criminal Law Journal. The factual aspects of the case are that M/s. cargo Chariot Company was appointed the carrier of different kinds of construction materials under Calcutta Construction Division in the year 1953-5.4. Thereafter, they were entrusted with a delivery order in respect of 100 tons of cement in their capacity as carrying contractor. They were asked to carry the cement from Pathuriaghat godown of Messrs Balmer Lawrie and Company to the Presidency General Hospital, Bhowanipore. When the cement was taken to the said hospital it was discovered that 120 bags containing 6 tons of cement did not contain genuine cement. An Information was accordingly lodged by Sri HN Gupta, Sub-Divisional Officer, Works and Building Department, PG Hospital, Sub-division No.2, with the Bhowanipore police on the 5th of May 1953. On 10th  August, 1953, the Investigating Inspector submitted a challan before the Police Magistrate, Alipore, against Niren, Nishit and Arun and two others persons Ranjit-Singha Roy and Provat Chandra Ghose alleging that they had committed and offence under section 407 of the Indian Penal Code. The same Investigating Officer submitted another challan before the same Magistrate against Ranjit and Provat alleging commission of an offence under section 7 of west Bengal Cement Control Act for having taken delivery of cement without any permit. The second case has ended in the discharge of the two accused. When the first case was going on before Sri SK Ganguly, Magistrate, 1 s class, Alipore, the prosecutor made a prayer under section 494 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for withdrawal of the case under section 407 IPC stating therein that the learned Magistrate had no jurisdiction to try the case and accordingly, the learned Magistrate discharged the accused from the case under section 494 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In the meantime, two witnesses for the prosecution appear to have been examined by this Magistrate. Then the case was started before a Magistrate at Sealdah. Before this Magistrate a question of Jurisdiction also appears to have been raised by the Public Prosecutor. The question of jurisdiction, however, that appears to have been raised here was of a different character from the one which was raised before the Magistrate at Alipore. Here, the question was whether an offence alleged to have been committed was one under section 409 IPC and triable by a Special Court set up under section 2 of the West Bengal Criminal Law Amendment (Special Courts) Act 1949. One behalf of the Prosecution, it was contended before him that the offence was one tinder section 409 IPC and was triable by a Special Court. On behalf of the defence; however, it was argued that it was an offence not under section 409 IPC at all but one under section 407 IPC arid, as such, it was triable by the Magistrate. The learned Magistrate, however, held prima-facie that the case was one under section 409 IPC and that it was triable by a Special Court. He accordingly directed the prosecution to take suitable steps with the State Government for allocation of the case to a Special Court. On the 22td of December 1954, the Public Prosecutor filed a petition before the Magistrate stating that the Government was of the view that the case was one under section 407 IPC so as to be triable by the Magistrate and the prosecution accordingly asked for date of hearing. The Magistrate then went on with the case. After hearing some witnesses, he discharged two of the accused Ranjit and Provat for lack of evidence and framed charges against Niren, Nishit and Arun. Thereafter, these three moved before the Sessions Judge,-and on transfer of the same, an Additional Sessions Judge made a criminal reference before Calcutta High Court. In the said criminal reference case of the State vs Niren Das Gupta reported in 1957 Cri LJ 124 (Volume 58 CN 40) (Calcutta High Court), it has been decided: 

 "Had it been the prosecution case that Messars. Cargo Chariot Company were appointed the carriers on one solitary occasion only, viz, when they were entrusted with the delivery order of 100 tons of cement the case would certainly have been one under section 407 IPC but when they were appointed carriers for the whole of the years 1953-54, they were appointed agents of Construction Division for that year for the carriage of building materials for the Construction Division for the year 1953-54, and, as such, carrying contractors or agents they were entrusted with the delivery of 100 tons of cements. That being so, prima-facie they were entrusted with dominion over 100 tons of cement in the way of their business as agents or carrying contractors of the Construction Division which is a department of the Government and criminal breach of trust is alleged to have been committed by them in respect of a part of these 100 tons of cement after they were entrusted with dominion over the same in the way of their business as an agent of a department of the State Government. That being so. Prima facie the case seems to be one under section 409 IPC and not one under section 407 IPC. Therefore the learned Magistrate was correct when he held on the 19th of June 1954 that it was a prima-facie case under section 409, IPC committed by the accused persons in respect of Government property over which they were entrusted with dominion in the way of their business as agents of the Government and so the case would be triable by the Special Court set up under section 2 of the West Bengal Criminal Law Amendment (Special Courts) Act, 1949." 

 28. When any contractor is appointed by any department of the Government for construction of any building, the contractor is termed as an agent of the concerned department of the Government. Furthermore, receiving the work order for construction of a bhaban by the contractor as an agent from any department of the Government is also an entrustment with property. Once the contactor as agent receives the work order for construction of a building, he is under obligation to hand over the same to the authority by constructing the same as per work order. Here, in the instant case, the accused-petitioner as agent received work order, took some payment against the bills from the Roads and High ways, misappropriated the public money and ultimately failed to hand over the bhaban to the authority by constructing the same in time as per work order. Accordingly, failure to perform the work as per work order by the contractor in a way of his business as an agent taking fraudulent mens rea to deceive the Government amounts to an offence of criminal breach of trust which is punishable under section 409 of the Penal Code. 

 29. Having considered all the aspects of the case, we are of the view that the accused-petitioner is an agent of the Roads and High Ways, since prima-facie he has committed criminal breach of trust in respect of the property as described in the work order in the way of his business as an agent in misappropriating the public money and in not handing over the bhaban to the authority by constructing the same in time as per work order. Since offence under section 409 is a schedule offence of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and the accused-petitioner is an agent of the Roads and High Ways, the offence allegedly committed by the accused-petitioner can be tried by a Special judge under the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 even in the absence of any public servant. Accordingly, the decision taken in the case of Moyna Miah vs State reported in 1985 BLD (AD) 99 is not applicable to the instant case. 

 30. In order to elaborate our discussions on this point, it will be profitable to quote section 5(1) along with schedule to the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 which runs as follows: 

 Schedule appended to the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 prescribes as follows: 

 31. We have stated earlier that there are 3 accused in the present case and out of 3 accused, 2 accused namely (1) Colonel Oli Ahmed (Rtd.), the then Minister (2) Nurul Anowar, Chairman of Harala Union Parishad were the public servants and the present accused-petitioner is not a public servant because he is a contractor. It is true that the case against accused Colonel Oli Ahmed case was withdrawn by the Government though the settled principle of law is that the criminal offence never abates and the impugned proceeding initiated against another co-accused Nurul Anowar was also quashed by a Division Bench of this Court, but the fact remains that the fate of the decisions in respect of2 accused is subject to judicial scrutiny by the higher forum. We find from the prosecution materials that the present accused-petitioner and 2 others were actively involved in the construction process of the bhaban and after performing some works, the accused in collaboration with each other misappropriated some money amounting to Taka 40,38,779. As per contention of the learned Advocate for the accused-petitioner, since there are no public servants in the present case because of the withdrawal and quashing of the proceeding, the proceeding under sections 409/109 of the penal, code against the present accused-petitioner who is admittedly not a public servant is not maintainable. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has laid emphasis on the decision in the case of Taslima Khatoon Chhanda vs State reported 17 BLC 277 wherein it has been held: 

 32. On the other hand, the contention of the learned Advocate for the Durniti Daman Commission is that though the case of one of the co-accused was quashed by a Division Bench of this Court, they were not made party to the case, and, as such, if they would have been made party to the case, the fate of the case would have been otherwise. However, they have instruction to proceed with the case taking recourse to law considering the facts and circumstances of the case. The submission of the learned Advocate for Anti- Corruption Commission is that though the case against Colonel Oli Ahmed (Rtd.) was withdrawn though it is now well-settled that the criminal offence never abates and the proceeding drawn against another accused Nurul Anowar was quashed, the same have not reached its finality unless the same are finally adjudicated and decided by the higher forum. Eventually, we have found that out of 3 accused, 2 accused were public servants. Now, we want to discuss some relevant laws including the schedules appended there-to since those have positive bearing on the issue. Section 5(2) of the prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 provides that any public servant who commits or attempts to commit criminal misconduct shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, or with time, or with both, and the pecuniary resources or property to which the Criminal misconduct relates may also be confiscated to the State. Section 5(1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 provides that notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, or in any other law, the offences specified in the Schedule shall be triable exclusively by a Special Judge. It appears from the schedule to the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 that the offences punishable under sections 161 to 166, 168, 217, 218, 403 to 409, 417 to 420, 465 to 468,471 and 477A of the Penal Code when committed by any public servant or by any person acting jointly with or a abetting or attempting to abet or acting in conspiracy with any public servant shall be tried under the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958: It maybe noted that the schedule appended to the Criminal Law Amendment Act,1958 has been substituted by the Criminal Law Amendment (Amendment) Act, 2004 (Act No. 22 of 2004). The present schedule to the aforesaid Act, 1958 runs as follows: 

 35. It is important to note that the prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 does not contain the procedure of trial of the offences punishable under this Act. The offences punishable under this act have been included in the schedule of the Criminal Law amendment Act, 1958 and they are triable by the Special Judge as contemplated in section 5 of the said Act. It appears from the FIR that the alleged occurrence occurred during the period from September, 1994 to June, 1995. It is evident from the schedule to the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 that the offence under section 409 of the Penal Code is a schedule offence which is triable by a Special Judge as provided in section 5 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. 

 37. We have gone through the decision taken in the case of Taslima Khatoon Chanda vs State reported in 17 BLC 277 wherein we have found that the accused-petitioners of that case were neither public servants nor agent of any department of the Government. We have also gone through the other decisions referred to by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. On going through all the decisions, we find that the facts and circumstances of those cases are quite distinguishable from the facts and circumstances of the present case. Accordingly, those decisions are not applicable to the present case.
